details: Every point in an eluder witness is active, and the points in a witness sequence are distinct.
proof: At each witnessing point the base and witness hypothesis disagree, so the point lies in the effective range. A repeated point cannot be independent after it has appeared, because agreement with the base on the earlier copy forces agreement at its later copy.
name: Effective Range / Combinatorial Eluder Dimension
witness_verification: For #classes/trivial_concepts with n>=4, the established endpoint values or bounds, in parameter order, are $n$ and $1$. The first parameter divided by one plus the second tends to infinity. Thus no reverse affine-linear bound holds. See the database-owned endpoint value proofs.
